::: {.profile-main}
I am the Director of Research and Chief Economist at the [International Growth Centre](https://www.theigc.org/) and a Research Fellow in the Department of Economics at the [London School of Economics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/). I hold a PhD in Economics from LSE.

My research sits at the intersection of development, environmental, and political economy. I study how energy systems, climate change, and new technologies shape structural transformation—and how institutions can manage those transitions more effectively. My work uses field experiments, administrative data, and quantitative models, with projects across South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa.

Alongside my academic work, I lead the IGC's global research portfolio and a team of more than twenty economists. I have advised governments across Asia and Africa on energy and public finance, including senior decision-makers in Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Myanmar.

The questions that motivate my work are analytically difficult and immediately consequential: how to design a power market that firms and households can rely on; how economies build new productive capabilities; and how people with the fewest resources can adapt to a changing climate.

## Research leadership

At the IGC, I help set research priorities and connect academic work to the questions facing policymakers in low- and middle-income countries. The portfolio spans sustainable growth, firms, cities, and state effectiveness across eleven country programmes in Africa, Asia, and the Middle East.

My own policy engagement has concentrated on electricity pricing and market design, fiscal reform, and the political economy of implementation. This work complements—not substitutes for—the academic research: each informs the questions, data, and institutional constraints of the other.
